gauntlet: question
A fits because the existing resolver already supplies this view's settings. `settings/resolver.ts:12` owns the defaults, every existing setting already flows through it, and I traced the resolved values into `ui/report-view.ts:30`, where the view reads them. A new key there needs no new loading or wiring, and the view keeps one source of truth. Option B would add a second settings path beside the resolver. Its default and its lifetime would have to stay in sync by hand, and the view would read from two places. I've recorded "settings ownership: existing resolver (`settings/resolver.ts:12`)" in the draft.

The open behavior is what happens to report filters when you switch workspaces. Today they stay active, which sometimes hides rows in the new workspace. What should the new setting control?
A) whether filters reset on workspace switch, defaulting to reset - fixes the hidden-rows problem out of the box, and users who want filters carried over can opt in
B) whether filters reset on workspace switch, defaulting to keep - current behavior stays the default, and only users who opt in get the fix
C) no setting for this: filters always reset on workspace switch, and the report-view setting covers something else - other - name it
Recommendation: A - the reported problem is filters hiding rows after a switch, so resetting by default fixes it, and the toggle keeps the old carry-over behavior for anyone who relies on it.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
gauntlet: question
Reusing the resolver fits because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. Adding the setting there preserves one source of truth and the existing resolver-to-view path; a view-local object would introduce a second settings owner.

What should happen to active report filters when switching workspaces?
A) Clear them so the new workspace starts unfiltered.
B) Preserve them, keeping the current behavior.
C) Restore each workspace’s own filters rather than carrying filters between workspaces.
D) Other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it directly prevents filters from the previous workspace from hiding rows in the new one, without introducing per-workspace filter storage.
